findings.finding: mseccfg reset only clears the register when ext_smepmp is active, but the CSR also exists when ext_zkr, ext_smmpm, or ext_zicfilp are enabled without smepmp. Per spec: norm:mseccfg_mml_mmwp_rlb_rst requires MML/MMWP/RLB reset to 0; norm:mseccfg_useed_sseed_rst requires USEED/SSEED have defined reset values; norm:mseccfg_mlpe_rst requires MLPE reset to 0; norm:warl_rst requires no WARL field contains an illegal value. If zkr/smmpm/zicfilp is enabled without smepmp, mseccfg retains stale values across reset, violating all these reset requirements.

spec_citations.excerpt: [#norm:mseccfg_mlpe_rst]#If the Zicfilp extension is implemented, the mseccfg.MLPE field is reset to 0.# [...] [#norm:mseccfg_mml_mmwp_rlb_rst]#The MML, MMWP, and RLB fields of the mseccfg register are set to 0, unless the platform mandates a different reset value.# [...] [#norm:mseccfg_useed_sseed_rst]#The USEED and SSEED fields of the mseccfg CSR must have defined reset values. The system must not allow them to be in an undefined state after reset.#
[#norm:warl_rst]#No WARL field contains an illegal value.#

findings.finding: have_mseccfg() does not check ext_zicfilp, but the new VMState mseccfg_needed() in machine.c does check it. If zicfilp were enabled without smepmp/zkr/smmpm, the CSR would be inaccessible (ILLEGAL_INST) but the VMState subsection would still activate, leading to inconsistency. In current profiles this doesn't trigger because zicfilp is only enabled alongside smepmp, but the mismatch is a maintenance hazard.

spec_citations.excerpt: [#norm:mseccfg_presence]#It exists if any extension that adds a field to mseccfg is implemented. Otherwise, it is reserved.#
[#norm:mseccfg_mlpe_presence]#The Zicfilp extension adds the MLPE field in mseccfg.#

findings.finding: The new vmstate_mseccfg subsection correctly identifies when mseccfg migration is needed by checking all four extensions that add fields to mseccfg (ext_smepmp, ext_zkr, ext_smmpm, ext_zicfilp). The VMSTATE_UINTTL correctly saves/restores the full register value. The subsection is properly registered in vmstate_riscv_cpu.subsections.

The mseccfg write path correctly enforces WARL sticky-bit semantics for MMWP/MML (once set cannot be unset until PMP reset), RLB (cannot be re-enabled when locked regions exist and RLB is 0), PMM (only writable with valid non-reserved values on RV64 with smmpm), and MLPE (forced to 1 when zicfilp is implemented). TLB flush is correctly triggered when MMWP/MML change.

spec_citations.excerpt: [#norm:mseccfg_rlb_op_warl]#When mseccfg.RLB is 0 and pmpcfg.L is 1 in any rule, then mseccfg.RLB remains 0 and any further modifications to mseccfg.RLB are ignored until a PMP reset.#

findings.finding: The mseccfg read path simply returns the cached env->mseccfg value, which is correct since all WARL filtering happens on write. No reserved bits leak since writes filter through the mask.
